business_problem: FastLabel needed to prepare large computer-vision datasets for autonomous-driving and industrial workloads, but manual captioning and duplicate review made image curation slow, expensive, and too error-prone to keep up with customer demand.
solution_summary: FastLabel built an image-data curation service on NVIDIA NeMo Curator running on NVIDIA A100 GPUs in Google Cloud Platform. The workflow starts with large autonomous-driving image sets and generates detailed domain-specific captions through vision-language models hosted on GCP. Those captions are embedded and then processed through NeMo Curator's semantic deduplication pipeline so the service can identify visually redundant examples that rule-based filters would miss. By turning image semantics into text, FastLabel made it practical to curate long-tail datasets for perception systems while drastically reducing manual review. The same pipeline now underpins FastLabel Data Curation, a productized service that produces automatically tagged, deduplicated image datasets faster, at lower cost, and with less wasted training compute for customers building autonomous and industrial vision models.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA A100
solution_components.role: Accelerates captioning, embedding, and deduplication workloads for large image sets.

solution_components.name: Google Cloud Platform
solution_components.role: Hosts the GPUs and supporting models used in FastLabel's curation pipeline.

solution_components.name: vision language models
solution_components.role: Generate domain-specific image captions that drive semantic deduplication.

data_flow: Raw image datasets are captioned by vision-language models on GCP, captions are embedded and passed into NeMo Curator on A100 GPUs, semantically similar examples are removed, and the cleaned datasets are delivered through FastLabel's data-curation service for downstream autonomous-vision training.
business_outcome: FastLabel reduced a 10,000-image captioning effort from 333 hours to 14.6 hours, ran text embedding and semantic deduplication in minutes, lowered the total cost of processing 10,000 images to under $57, and used the pipeline to launch its commercial FastLabel Data Curation service.
